## TL;DR

Review round 2 found one more place where text never wraps: the dev-update dialog's commit notes. They come from a remote `latest.json`, so they are not fixed copy. I added `overflow-wrap: anywhere` to `.update-dialog`, which the heading, paragraphs and list items inherit. The table test now pins that selector too. Review also said the QA claims could not be rerun from the branch, so I committed the measurement harness as `mobile/scripts/fixture-qa.ts`. It runs 25 checks. All pass with the fix, and six wrapping checks plus the dialog bounds check fail when the rules are stripped. The QA doc's claims are now tied to those checks. Device QA (#1162) and iOS are still unverified and need a human.

## Work and rationale

Round 2 claimed the rest of the hub's text was fixed copy or ellipsis-truncated. That was wrong for the dev-update dialog. `App.vue` renders each note from `devUpdate.notes` in an `<li>`, and `dev-updates.ts` reads those notes from a remote manifest. The notes are filled from task titles, so an unbroken token is possible. I'd checked the picker, sheet, discovery and form paths, not this dialog. The fix is a single declaration on `.update-dialog`, because `overflow-wrap` is inherited. I put a comment on the rule explaining the remote source.

For reproducibility I moved the measurement code out of scratch. `mobile/scripts/fixture-qa.ts` runs the seven fixture routes, checks that no element extends past 375px, checks the console, and runs the interaction and long-text cases. It uses `@playwright/test`, which the repo's browser tests already import. A `QA_STRIP_WRAP=1` switch removes the wrapping declarations from the served stylesheet, so a reader can see the checks fail. The wrap cases rewrite the served fixture or inject elements with the shell's real class names. The dialog is injected because the sweep never fetches the remote manifest that opens it.

I corrected the QA doc in three places. The Setup section now points to the script and explains why element bounds are used instead of page `scrollWidth`. The re-run section describes the script and the stripped negative run. The "not covered" list no longer says the dev-update dialog is untested, and now says its real trigger is not exercised.

Round 2 wrote `docs/qa/...:62` as closed at four selectors. The doc now lists five: the sheet URL, the discovery message, the form warning, the failure reason, and the dialog notes. It also records `.form-error` as not reachable with unbroken text, since its strings are fixed copy.

## Approaches tried

The first version of the harness was a scratch Playwright file with the measurements inline. It proved the numbers but could not be rerun from the branch, which is the reviewer's complaint. I turned it into a committed script with a pass or fail line per check and an exit code, so a failure is visible without reading screenshots.

For the dialog I considered forcing the real trigger by editing the manifest URL. The dialog depends on a dev-update config that the sweep does not set up, so injecting the shell's own markup was the more faithful test of the CSS. The doc says so.

I did not commit screenshots. The script prints measurements, which are the evidence, and binary files under `docs/` would add noise without adding checks.

## Challenges and blockers

Two runs of the new script needed care. The first run used a dev server I had started on `localhost`. The script's default base URL matches that port, so a missing server would show up as failed checks rather than a silent pass. I confirmed the server's working directory before running and stopped only that process afterward.

The negative run is what makes the script trustworthy. A harness that only passes proves little. With the rules stripped, six wrap checks and the dialog bounds check fail. The picker and row checks still pass, which is correct, because they depend on the `.server-row` fix and not on wrapping.

The wrapper run passes 21 mobile and hub files and 203 tests. That count includes one new table case, for `.update-dialog`. The scoped repo check passes on every step.

## Key learnings

When a review says a class is "closed", list every instance by searching the code, not by reading the reported ones. Round 2 closed the class by sampling and missed the dialog, which is the only text in the hub that comes from outside the app.

A measurement that is not committed is not evidence for a reviewer. Put the harness in the repo, make it print one line per check, and give it a mode that is expected to fail.

`overflow-wrap` is inherited, so a declaration on a container covers its children. That made the dialog fix one line, but the comment is needed so the next reader does not add the same declaration to every child.

Two items still need a human. Real-device QA on Android (#1162) cannot be replaced by this run. The sweep also has no `?fixture=error` route, so the error paths depend on the scripted interactions.
